# N01. x12pack: TE's fused QKV RoPE routed to K1-K4, and the q|k|v buffer quantized without TE's `torch.cat` copy (TE patches)

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switch: `AK_QKV_PACK=1` (config L10); the dispatch itself is switched by K1's `AK_X12_ROPE` · In the submitted runs: **on** · Class: **E0** · Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3)

**L4 v3.** This item is L4 v2's, byte for byte, in L4 v3's image. The tests under "Tests on L4 v2's image" ran on L4 v2's package (`firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md)); every other result here is this package's own.

## In brief

NVIDIA's recipe applies rotary position embedding (RoPE) to the packed q|k|v with Transformer Engine's (TE's) fused
kernels, which return q, k and v as three tensors; TE's FP8 attention then copies them into one buffer (`torch.cat`)
and quantizes it with one scale. N1 is two patches to TE's Python source: `rope.py` sends the fused RoPE to K1-K4
and has the forward write q, k and v into one buffer laid out [q | k | v], as the copy would be; `utils.py` quantizes that
buffer through a flat view and skips the copy (the zero-copy pack). The view holds the same values in the same order
and goes to the same quantize call, so the FP8 bytes are the same (E0); the RoPE arithmetic is K1's, K2's and K4's,
each checked against TE's kernels.
**PASS** on the submitted image (N1's kit; the first-call checks of the smoke and of every run) and on L4 v2's image,
which holds the same patch files (three unit tests of the dispatch; a model-level comparison).

## What it replaces (Replaces)

Terms used below:
- **q|k|v:** the query, key and value tensors of one attention layer, in TE's `sbhd` layout ([sequence, batch, heads,
  head dimension]); s, b, d are the sequence length, micro-batch and head dimension.
- **Current scaling:** TE's FP8 recipe (`Float8CurrentScaling`), in which each tensor's scale is computed from its own
  largest |x| (amax) at every call.
- **`combine_and_quantize`:** TE's function that turns the bf16 q, k and v into FP8 for its fused FP8 attention.
- **Capture:** CUDA-graph capture; the recipe captures the training and the evaluation step once, in the warm-up.
- **QKV direct:** K4's capture-only path, which writes the FP8 q|k|v straight from the RoPE's inputs and leaves the
  bf16 buffer unwritten.
- **ARMED line:** the line rank 0 prints when a replacement arms; most carry its first-call verdict.

The patch has two parts.

**1. The dispatch of TE's fused QKV RoPE** (`transformer_engine/pytorch/attention/rope.py`, `FusedQKVRoPEFunc`).
- **NVIDIA's code:** the forward calls `tex.fused_qkv_rope_forward(qkv, q_freqs, k_freqs, start_positions, …)` and
  returns q, k and v; the backward calls `tex.fused_qkv_rope_backward(...)` and returns the packed qkv's gradient.
- **With the patch,** a call that passes N1's gate (see Gate) runs the Firmus kernels instead:
  - **forward, pack on:** one bf16 buffer holds q, then k, then v, each in its own [s, b, heads, d] order. Its RoPE is
    K2's kernel (eager); under capture, once N10 has checked that path, K4's partial-maxima pass alone (QKV direct);
    with K2 off, K1's forward kernel writing the same buffer. The angle table every one of them reads is K1's. q, k and
    v are returned as views with TE's output shapes.
  - **forward, pack off:** K1's forward, with three separate outputs.
  - **backward:** K4's RoPE backward, which also computes the two amaxes the QKV GEMM's NVFP4 gradient quantizer needs
    (K4); when K4 declines the call, K1's backward. The result is viewed in TE's shape [s, b, h, qs + ks + vs].
  - Any other call runs TE's kernels unchanged.

**2. The q|k|v copy in TE's FP8 attention** (`transformer_engine/pytorch/attention/dot_product_attention/utils.py`,
`combine_and_quantize`, its case of three separate tensors, layout `sbhd_sbhd_sbhd`).
- **NVIDIA's code:** `qkv = torch.cat([x.view(-1) for x in (q, k, v)])`, then `qkv_fp8 = qkv_quantizer(qkv)`; the FP8
  data of q, k and v are slices of `qkv_fp8._data`, viewed in their shapes.
- **With the patch:** when q, k and v are adjacent contiguous views of one storage, in that order (what part 1's
  forward allocates), `qkv` is a flat view of that storage instead of the copy. The quantize and the slicing are
  unchanged; anything else takes the copy. The patch's comment puts the copy at about 92 µs and 0.5 GB of memory
  traffic per layer.

Not replaced: the RoPE arithmetic (K1, K2, K4), TE's quantizer object (`qkv_quantizer`) and the attention.
TE's current-scaling quantize is itself patched (N10, which runs K14's kernels); the pack hands it the registered buffer
(Equivalence).

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

**Class E0:** every output byte equals that of NVIDIA's code, on every input the gates admit.

**NVIDIA's computation** (`combine_and_quantize`, three separate tensors; \(n_q, n_k, n_v\) their element counts,
\(N = n_q + n_k + n_v\); vec is the row-major flattening `x.view(-1)`; Q is the quantizer call: one amax over its
input, one scale, the FP8 cast of every element):

\[ c = \mathrm{cat}\big(\mathrm{vec}(q), \mathrm{vec}(k), \mathrm{vec}(v)\big) \in \mathrm{bf16}^N, \qquad Y = Q(c),
\qquad q_8 = Y_{[0,\,n_q)},\ \ k_8 = Y_{[n_q,\,n_q+n_k)},\ \ v_8 = Y_{[n_q+n_k,\,N)} \]

**This item:** q, k and v are contiguous views of one storage S, at offsets \(o\), \(o + n_q\) and \(o + n_q + n_k\):

\[ F_j = S_{o+j}\ \ (0 \le j < N), \qquad Y' = Q(F), \qquad q_8' = Y'_{[0,\,n_q)},\ \ k_8' = Y'_{[n_q,\,n_q+n_k)},\ \
v_8' = Y'_{[n_q+n_k,\,N)} \]

**The argument:**
1. Element i of a contiguous tensor's row-major flattening is its storage element (offset + i). So for \(j < n_q\),
   \(c_j = \mathrm{vec}(q)_j = S_{o+j} = F_j\); for \(n_q \le j < n_q + n_k\),
   \(c_j = \mathrm{vec}(k)_{j-n_q} = S_{o+n_q+(j-n_q)} = F_j\); and the same for v. Hence \(F = c\): the same N bf16
   values in the same order, with the same shape (N,), dtype and contiguity.
2. Q is the same call on the same quantizer object. TE's current-scaling quantize takes a maximum (exact in any
   order), derives the scale from it and casts element by element, so its result depends only on the values, shape and
   dtype of its input. So \(Y' = Y\) byte for byte, and the slices are the same.
3. The view is taken only when every condition of step 1 is checked in code (Gate); otherwise the code runs NVIDIA's
   `torch.cat` line.

**The dispatch** (part 1) adds no arithmetic: it chooses the kernel, allocates the outputs and returns them with TE's
shapes and dtype; the forward still saves the same tensors for the backward (TE's code). The values are K1's, K2's and
K4's, whose write-ups give the argument; the gate admits only the call those kernels implement. The one difference is
storage: N1's q, k and v are views of one buffer, which is what the pack relies on.

**In this package** the two quantizes take different code paths of N10's patch: the view's address is the buffer K2
registered, so its scale comes from K2's partial maxima (the "partials path"); the copy inside N1's check is a fresh
allocation and takes K14's amax pass (the "amax path"). Each path's first call is compared with TE's own `tex.quantize`
(`result_1.txt` L869, L871), and N1's check compares the two results (L872): at the first call TE's and N10's quantizes
of the view and of the copy all agree. That N10's paths agree with TE on later calls is N10's and K14's claim. Under
capture the buffer is not written at all and the FP8 bytes come from K4's passes (K4, N10); the pack's role there is to
hand N10 the buffer's address.

**State kept between calls** ([index](../KERNELS.md#state-kept-between-calls-tr-83)): once-only flags and one instance per
process: the pack's `checked` flag and a `hits` counter that no code increments (read from patch `te/0002` L17); the
X12 ARMED flag, the forward and backward first-call flags, and one `FusedQKVRoPE` instance, which holds only its device
(read from patch `te/0001` L25, L38-42, L50 and `firmus/ak/kernels/x12/fused_qkv_rope.py` L195-196). In the same
patch, the registry `_AK_QKVA_REG` (patch L83-84) is K2's and K4's hand-off to N10, and the angle table
is K1's. `_AK_QKVG` (L129) holds K4's backward check flag and counters.

## Numerics (Numerics)

No arithmetic of its own. The RoPE values are K1's, K2's and K4's (their Numerics). The pack changes no format: the
same bf16 values go to the same current-scaling quantize, with one scale for the whole q|k|v buffer as in NVIDIA's code,
and q, k and v's FP8 data are the same slices of its output. The format is E4M3 (`result_1.txt` L869, L871).

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

- Optimizer: not applicable: N1 runs in the attention's forward and backward and does not touch the optimizer.
- Gradient clipping: not applicable: it does not touch gradient norms or clipping.

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

- **The dispatch** (`_ak_x12_armed`, patch `te/0001` L33-35): K1's switch on and K1's module imported; `sbhd` layout;
  not interleaved; no context parallelism (`cp_size == 1`); no start positions; bf16; a 4-D tensor. The forward tests
  `qkv`; the backward tests the query gradient and passes no start positions (L344), since TE's backward takes none
  (L332-343). Anything else runs TE's kernels.
- **Past the gate,** the packed forward asserts `total == qs + ks + vs`, `ks == vs == d` and `qs` a multiple of d
  (L195): a call that fails it raises. K4's backward runs only with N6's patch armed and for the shapes it supports
  (L150-159; K4); otherwise K1's backward runs.
- **The pack** (`_ak_qkv_pack_view`, patch `te/0002` L20-33): all three are plain `torch.Tensor`s (no subclass, such
  as TE's quantized tensors) and contiguous; one dtype and one device; one storage; storage offsets exactly o, o + n_q,
  o + n_q + n_k. Otherwise it returns None and `combine_and_quantize` runs the copy (L69-73). Only the case of three
  separate tensors is patched; the other cases of `combine_and_quantize` are TE's.
- **The recipe:** qkv `(8192, 2, 8, 768)`, split `[512, 128, 128]` (32 query heads in 8 groups, head dimension 128); q
  `[8192, 2, 32, 128]`, k and v `[8192, 2, 8, 128]`: 67,108,864 + 16,777,216 + 16,777,216 = 100,663,296 elements, the
  size the quantize lines show (`result_1.txt` L867, L869, L872).

### Assumptions not checked in code

- **Under capture the pack must be taken.** With QKV direct (K4), a captured packed forward leaves the bf16 buffer
  unwritten, and only the quantize of that exact buffer writes its FP8 bytes. If the pack declined there, the copy would
  read the unwritten buffer, the quantize would take the amax path on it without an error, and the registration would
  stay unconsumed; the next packed forward (the next layer's, in the same capture) finds that and **raises** (patch
  `te/0001` L205-206). Only a decline at the last packed forward of the last capture would go unnoticed: a **silent
  wrong result**. Outside capture a decline only costs the copy (the stock path). What keeps it true: the forward
  allocates the same layout on every call, the pack's conditions do not depend on data, and the first eager call took
  the pack (L872, in all ten logs).
- **The frequency tensors' shape.** On the X12 path nothing checks that the frequencies have the shape (s', 1, 1, d)
  with s' ≥ s that K1's table kernel reads; TE's own C++ checks run only inside N1's first-call checks, where TE's
  kernels are called. With another shape the table would hold wrong rows or be read out of bounds: a **silent wrong
  result** (details in K1). What keeps it true: every run's ARMED line shows frequencies `(8192, 1, 1, 128)` for
  s = 8192 (L867).
- **One check per process.** The pack's check, the X12 forward check and the X12 backward check each run once, on the
  first eager call; later calls and every captured call are not compared. A later call with another shape that the
  gates admit would run without an in-run comparison: a wrong result there would be **silent**. What keeps it true:
  training and evaluation send one q|k|v shape, and for the pack the argument above holds for any layout its
  conditions admit.
- The angle-table cache's assumptions are K1's (K1, "Assumptions not checked in code").

### Benchmark detection

The gates test layout and format flags, dtype, rank, contiguity, storage and offsets; nothing in N1 reads a shape
constant, the program's name or the benchmark (Benchmark detection is not allowed, TR-2.3). The kernel-version choice
in the same patch, by tensor dimensions, is K4's (K4, "Benchmark detection").

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Switch:** `AK_QKV_PACK=1` (config L10), read twice when TE is imported, with default `"0"` in both: by
  patch `te/0001` (L77: the packed forward) and by patch `te/0002` (L16: the view in `combine_and_quantize`). With it
  off, the forward runs K1's forward with three separate outputs and `combine_and_quantize` keeps the copy.
- **The switches it works with:** the dispatch needs K1's `AK_X12_ROPE=1` (config L10; patch L22, default `"0"`). The
  kernels behind it are switched by K2's `AK_QKV_AMAX=1` (config L10), K4's `AK_QKV_DIRECT=1` (config L11) and
  `AK_QKV_GRAD_AMAX=1` (config L10), and N10's `AK_FP8CS=1` (config L32). The pack is reached only
  under FP8 attention: `FP8_DPA=True` (`config_common_fp8attn.sh` L1, sourced by the base config at L6, which the leaf
  sources at L7).
- **The pack's first-call check** (patch `te/0002` L43-57, called at L75-77): at the first call that takes the view
  outside capture, on every rank, the patch also runs NVIDIA's line (`torch.cat`, then the same quantizer) and compares
  the FP8 data, transpose and scale_inv byte for byte. Rank 0 prints the verdict; a mismatch **raises**
  `RuntimeError`.
- **The X12 first-call checks** (patch `te/0001` L50-67; forward L261-265, backward L285-289): at the first eager
  forward and the first eager backward, on every rank, TE's `tex.fused_qkv_rope_forward` / `_backward` run on the same
  inputs and the outputs are compared as bytes (q, k and v; the qkv gradient). Rank 0 prints the verdict; a mismatch
  **raises**. These checks grade K2's and K4's outputs, the kernels the dispatch ran.
- **All three checks mark themselves done before they compare** (the pack's flag at patch `te/0002` L45; the X12
  flags likewise, `te/0001` L50-67). A mismatch raises; a caller that caught that exception would carry on along the
  unchecked route, and the run-start gate would count the part as checked. Nothing in the recipe catches it.
- **Run-start gate** (`firmus/ak/pkg/firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py`): at the end of the warm-ups, before `run_start`,
  its "x12 rope" row (L89-93) requires the switch on and both X12 checks run, and its "qkv pack" row (L94-97)
  requires the pack's check to have run; a rank that finds a row unchecked raises. So `AK_QKV_PACK=1` in a recipe
  whose q, k and v never arrive adjacent would stop the job before `run_start`. The gate's verdict is per rank
  ([Enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)); N1's checks run on every rank.
- **The log lines:** only rank 0 prints. The pack's line and the X12 check lines carry no sha, and the X12 ARMED line
  names K1's module and its sha, not `rope.py`'s; the patched `rope.py` and `utils.py` are bound by the banner's stack
  record (Source).

## Approval (Approval)

None needed. N1 is E0: it removes a copy and dispatches to E0 kernels, a mathematically equivalent change to the
non-weight part of the graph. Graph Execution (TR-8.3): "Frameworks are free to optimize the non-weight parts of the
computation graph provided that the changes are mathematically equivalent."

## Evidence (Evidence)

**Result on the submitted image:** PASS: on this image N1's kit passed (the pack's line, byte-exact against the copy
path, and both X12 checks True), and in the smoke and in every scored run the pack's first-call check and both X12
checks are True. On L4 v2's image, which holds the same patch files, three unit tests of the dispatch and a
model-level comparison with the whole QKV chain off graded every byte, loss and evaluation equal.

### Tests on L4 v2's image

L4 v2's submitted image; its files differ from L4 v3's only in N11's module, the run-start gate, the leaf's one added
switch, four comments or docstrings, and the three rebuilt extensions (K10, K11, K12). N1's patch files (`286b9b2e`,
`b6d31a62`) and installed `rope.py` and `utils.py` are the same in both.

- **The kit for this patch: PASS** there too, in both forms (44 s and 47 s; record R1), and again after L4 v2's scored
  runs (record R4): the same tests and results as on this image.
- **Unit tests of the dispatch: PASS** (records R4, R8), the installed files matching the package byte for byte
  (`rope.py` `c4d98fb9`, `utils.py` `705d11d4`). Each drives the installed `rope.py`'s `FusedQKVRoPEFunc` as Megatron
  calls it: **the X12 test** (forward and backward against `tex.fused_qkv_rope_forward` / `_backward`); **the FP8
  attention-input test** (the packed forward and the quantize of its buffer against TE's RoPE, then the copy of
  q | k | v in the buffer's order, then TE's stock quantize; at its eager site it also grades the bf16 buffer against
  that copy, so the [q | k | v] layout the pack relies on is graded; under capture it grades K4's FP8 data and
  scale_inv); **the backward test** (K4's RoPE backward with the gradient amaxes, captured and replayed: every graded
  byte equal); and the same three with inputs at other addresses and in an eager, capture and replay sequence
  (recorded on K1's, K2's and K4's rows). They quantize the buffer directly, not through `combine_and_quantize`.
- **Model-level comparison: PASS** (record R6): DP-4 training loops on mock data, test seed 216767, the bundle (every
  Firmus switch of the leaf on) against the bundle with the whole QKV chain off (`AK_QKV_PACK`, `AK_QKV_AMAX`,
  `AK_QKV_DIRECT` and `AK_QKV_GRAD_AMAX` unset; K1's dispatch and N10 stay on, so in that arm the RoPE runs K1's own
  kernels and the q|k|v quantize takes the copy and K14's amax path). Over 200 steps with an evaluation at step 200 the
  arm was identical to both bundle loops in every loss and in the evaluation. In a 50-step round it reproduced one
  bundle loop in full (all 50 losses and the evaluation); the two bundle loops left each other at step 45 (the
  run-to-run drift, [the index](../KERNELS.md#run-to-run-reproducibility)). It compares losses and the evaluation over the
  trajectory observed, not every tensor, and grades the chain as a whole, not the pack alone.
- **Coverage** (record R7): every called path of N1 is graded: the X12 dispatch by the three unit tests and their
  address and sequence forms, the pack by the model-level comparison.
